newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI net dollar purchase at $1.39 bln in May.
newsitem.headline: India RBI net dollar purchase at $1.39 bln in May.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Tuesday its net dollar purchases in May 1997 amounted to $1.39 billion, equivalent to 49.60 billion rupees.
Dollar purchases in May were $1.76 billion and sales $366 million, the Reserve Bank of India Bulletin for July 1997 said.
Cumulative dollar purchases in May 1997 (over end March 1996 figure) amounted to $2.03 billion, the bulletin said.
This cost the central bank 72.57 billion rupees.
Outstanding net forward dollar purchases in May 1997 amounted to $112 million, the bulletin said.
Analysts said RBI's dollar purchases, to arrest the rupee's rise on the back of large capital flows into the country, was increasing money supply in the banking system.
According to latest RBI data, M3 money supply growth on June 20, 1997 rose to 16.8 percent from 16.6 percent on June 6 and 15.5 percent a year ago.
RBI has set a target of keeping M3 growth at 15.0-15.5 percent in financial year 1997/98 (April-March).
